Synopsis:
A completely optional dialog with Barcus after the outcome of the Steel Watch Foundry has concluded. After the other gnomes leave Barcus sticks around until the next long rest. He looks at the burning Foundry and will react to what decisions you have made.

Cluster Contexts:
- LOW_SteelWatchFoundry_Barcus_AfterOutcome.json: You encounter Barcus after the Steel Watch Foundry sequence, when the other gnomes have already left and he remains beside the burning Foundry until the next long rest. Off‑screen the Foundry’s neural switchboard/Control Centre and the city’s tensions (Steel Watchers, Iron Throne remnants, Zhentarim, and rescued NPCs like Volo) explain why the area is dangerous and why people reacted strongly to the outcome; Barcus will respond to whatever choices you made with the Neurocitor. He is grieving a close companion named Wulbren — he speaks of following Wulbren through many dangers and feels guilt or helplessness over Wulbren’s death. The player can answer sympathetically or harshly (e.g., saying Wulbren “deserved” it or was “past saving”), which colors Barcus’s emotional reactions in this optional exchange.
- LOW_SteelWatchFoundry_Outcome.json: This scene takes place immediately after the player’s actions at the Steel Watch Foundry: the Neurocitor / lowest‑floor control centre that links the city’s Steel Watchers has been tampered with and Watchers are collapsing in the streets. Wulbren Bongle appears triumphant and vengeful, representing angry city survivors who view all Gondians as complicit, while Gondian workers (Menalda and possibly Toobin or a Gondian backup) plead that they were forced by the Banites/Iron Throne and beg for mercy. The player and a few surviving gnomes are on‑scene, catching their breath as Wulbren shifts from smug gratitude to a vow to eradicate every Gondian. Barchus and Toobin may be dead in some outcomes (or absent/replaced), and off‑screen factional tensions (Iron Throne remnants, Zhentarim middlemen, and Volo’s recent rescue) help explain why this confrontation is fraught and decisive.
- WYR_GortashConfrontation_OM_KarlachAndGortashEncounter_AOM_OOM.json: Dialog with Gortash in his office.Possible outcomes:1. You visited Steel Foundry and the destroyed Control Centre - he attacks you.2. You visited Steel Foundry, didn't destroy the Control Centre, but someone activated Dead Man switch which destroyed Iron T hrone. He attacks you.3. You visited Iron Throne which caused the destruction of it. He tells you - "I warned you" and then attacks you.4. You didn't kill Orin.5. You killed Orin and you have both Netherstones.6. Fallback node which includes the case where you killed Orin, but didn't bring either of the netherstones.
- LOW_SteelWatchFoundry_Confrontation_AfterIRN.json: This dialog plays if the player solves the Iron Throne before ever seeing the LOW_SteelWatchFoundry_DeadMansSwitchThreat dialog.After destroying the Iron Throne the player walks in Baneites tormenting Gondian Workers in the Foundry Work room.With the Iron Throne gone, the dead mans switch no longer works.
- WYR_KillDirectorGortash_GortashInOffice.json: You are confronting Lord Enver Gortash in his office after a bargain over the Netherstones; he physically checks his gauntlet for a resonance and expects you to have recovered Orin’s (and possibly Thorm’s) stone. Off‑screen you may have been down in the Steel Watch Foundry, dealing with the Neurocitor / Control Centre on the lowest floor — a Gondian–illithid neural switchboard whose destruction or activation (including a Dead‑Man trigger) can cause the Iron Throne’s collapse or wider Watcher cascades. Whether Orin lives or dies and whether you actually carry one or both Netherstones determines Gortash’s reaction: no resonance = betrayal, his “the brain awakens” threat, and in most branches he immediately attacks. Other background probes (Speak With Dead on Gortash’s parents, rescuing locals like Obelia, or saving Volo) may have already informed you about motives and the Foundry’s danger, but the scene hinges on the Iron Throne/Neurocitor outcomes and your possession of the stones.

Dialogue Excerpts (up to 3 samples, ordered):
Sample 1:
- Barcus Wroot: So many dead. Gondians. Ironhands... Wulbren. This wasn't supposed to happen. (node 8)
- Player: Wulbren deserved to die. (node 7)

Sample 2:
- Barcus Wroot: I followed him through the city, to the wilds, through the Underdark, and back home again. Braved goblins, shades, and evils I could hardly describe. || [context] NodeContext: sad (node 50)
- Barcus Wroot: Still, I couldn't save Wulbren from himself. I don't think anyone could. || [context] NodeContext: sad - wulbren is dead (node 53)
- Player: Wulbren was past saving. (node 51)

context: You find Barcus alone beside the burning Steel Watch Foundry after the main Foundry sequence; the other gnomes have already left and he stayed until the next long rest. Off‑screen the Foundry’s neural switchboard/Control Centre (the Neurocitor) has been tampered with, Watchers are collapsing in the streets, and surviving factional tensions (Iron Throne remnants, Steel Watchers, Zhentarim, rescued civilians like Volo) make the scene fraught. Barcus is grieving a close companion, Wulbren, whom he followed through many dangers and now feels guilt and helplessness over losing. The player’s earlier choices about the Neurocitor and whether Wulbren lived or died shape this optional exchange, and the player can answer sympathetically or harshly (e.g., “deserved” or “past saving”), which colors Barcus’s emotional responses.
